rationale: PY-29, second behaviour. `python/interface-implements` already pins that a base spelled `abc.ABC` is the stdlib class whatever else the file binds the bare name to, and that a BARE marker is resolved positionally against the bindings. Neither row can falsify the SUBSCRIPT case, because in that file the bare name `Protocol` is bound to the stdlib by `from typing import Protocol` on every line a subscripted base appears on — so the qualified reading and the bare reading agree, and a fixture built that way cannot tell which one produced the edge. This file removes the agreement by construction: it imports `typing` and does NOT import `Protocol` from it, and it declares a LOCAL `class Protocol` at line 33. `Protocol[RuntimeT]` is a `subscript` node whose head is `dotted_name("typing.Protocol")`, and the pre-pass read "qualified" as `b.type === "attribute"`, which classified that head as a BARE name. So the two readings now disagree on both sides of the file: the qualified one says `QualifiedProtocolBase` declares an interface (CPython: metaclass `_ProtocolMeta`, `_is_protocol=True`, and `QualifiedProtocolBase()` is refused with "Protocols cannot be instantiated"), and the bare one says the base is the local class three lines above and nothing is declared. `extractClass` already read the same subscript head as qualified for `qualifiedBases` — the same rule one position over, in the same file — so the pre-pass was the odd spelling out and this fixture is what makes the difference observable. `QualifiedAbcBase(typing.Generic[RuntimeT])` is the control: a qualified subscript head that is NOT an interface marker must produce no edge, so a mutant that simply treats every dotted head as an interface marker is caught as well as one that treats every dotted head as bare.

forbidRelationships.note: PY-34 (ruling 2026-10-09). THIS ROW WAS AN EXPECT when the file was merged, called ADDITIVE, on the reasoning that `issubclass(QualifiedProtocolBase, typing.Protocol)` is True and `Protocol` is in its `__mro__`, so a second edge was needed to keep the inheritance fact. It is now a forbid: that fact is published where the store WALKS it — `metadata.superTypes` from the FULL base list, copied into `brain_symbol.super_types`, read by `member-owner-resolution` and `override-retarget` — while the relationship label stays the most specific true one, exactly as `python/implements-interface-bases` forbids `extends FromAbc -> ABC` and for the same reason. The row's second justification was refuted by the code it appealed to: `extractOverrideRelationships` builds its MRO walk from `ctx.basesByClassKey`, the class's recorded base list, and only falls back to a name-keyed table built from `extends` rows when no owner declaration was recorded, so no override derivation loses anything when this edge is not emitted.

_seamNote.what: "Qualified" means the SOURCE spelled the marker with a module: `b.type === "attribute"`, or a `subscript` whose head is an `attribute`. It is read from the header, not from what the name happens to be bound to.
_seamNote.why: A dotted spelling names a module, so `typing.Protocol[RuntimeT]` is the stdlib class whatever this file binds the bare name to — and `typing.Generic[RuntimeT]`, read the same way, is not a marker at all. The two halves are the same predicate over two different heads, so reading the subscript head is not an extension of the rule but the rule applied consistently: `extractClass` already derives `qualifiedBases` this way for the override resolver's "a base spelled qualified is a class this file has not read" test, and two spellings of one predicate in one file is how they drift apart.
